name: Yard
notes: North Murfreesboro new build, tall fescue. Central Basin floor on Stones River limestone (karst / cedar glade country). Consequences: expect HIGH soil P (skip starter fertilizer; use 16-0-8 not 16-4-8; unneeded P on karst drains to groundwater), pH near neutral to alkaline near foundation (do NOT lime by habit; yellowing in high-pH zones = iron chlorosis, treat with foliar iron, not fertilizer), bedrock may be shallow and uneven (screwdriver test: zones that fail 4 inches brown first in July, green first in September -- give them extra compost topdress, do NOT chase with irrigation). Soil thermometer at 2 inches, morning reading 3 consecutive days, settles all timing; GreenCast soil temp map as remote proxy; daily_high is the trigger proxy here. Fall pre-emergent only in NON-overseed years -- skipped 2026 because overseeding. Fungicide window mid-June to early September when nights hold above 68F. Baseline culture: mow tall, water deep and infrequent, no feeding until soil temps start falling.

activities.name: UT Soil Test
activities.description: Sample now (July) so results set the September fertilizer plan. Collect 10-12 cores at 4 inches, front and back lawns as separate samples. Drop at Rutherford County Extension, Lane Agri-Park on John R. Rice Blvd (lab: soillab.tennessee.edu). The only decision-sensitive item before September.

steps.name: Pick up soil test boxes and forms at Extension office
Review soil test results and set fall fertilizer plan
steps.description: Expect high P (Central Basin phosphatic limestone): if confirmed, 16-0-8 for fall, no starter at overseed. Expect near-neutral pH: no lime unless the test explicitly calls for it.

activities.name: Confirm Water Utility & Irrigation Schedule
activities.description: North Murfreesboro splits between Murfreesboro Water Resources and Consolidated Utility District by annexation line. Confirm which one bills the house, check their odd/even summer irrigation schedule, then program the controller so cycle-and-soak fits inside allowed days.

activities.name: Spot-Spray Dallisgrass & Johnsongrass
activities.description: Construction fill here reliably imports dallisgrass and johnsongrass with the nutsedge. No pre-emergent touches dallisgrass and nothing selective kills it cleanly in fescue since MSMA left the residential market. Spot-spray glyphosate on a windless day while the clumps are few -- waiting a year turns a 10-minute job into a renovation. Kill spots get reseeded in September.

steps.name: Buy glyphosate and a small pump sprayer
Flag sprayed spots for September reseed

activities.name: Summer Fungicide Watch
activities.description: Brown patch window opens when evening temps hold above ~68F with humidity (mid-June through early September here). This is a watch, not an automatic application: scout weekly, treat only if disease shows and spreads.

activities.name: Armyworm Scouting
activities.description: Middle TN gets episodic fall armyworm waves in August-September (2021 was a local massacre), and a freshly germinated September overseed is their favorite meal. Soap-flush weekly from mid-August: 2 tbsp dish soap in 1 gal water over a square foot, count what surfaces. If larvae show, treat with bifenthrin or spinosad the SAME DAY -- hours matter, not days.

steps.name: Have bifenthrin or spinosad on hand

activities.name: Aerate, Overseed & Compost Topdress
activities.description: Prime window Sept 5 - Oct 1, HARD STOP Oct 15 (seedlings need 6+ weeks before real cold). Trigger: soil cooling into the 60s (daily highs holding at/below 85 as proxy). Compost topdress compounds annually -- give shallow-bedrock zones extra. No starter fertilizer if soil test confirmed high P.

steps.name: Order tall fescue seed
steps.description: Quality blends sell out by September -- order early

steps.name: Reserve core aerator and order compost
Flag irrigation heads and shallow-bedrock zones
steps.description: Screwdriver test: anywhere it won't go 4 inches down gets extra compost

steps.name: Begin light watering 2x daily until germination
First mow of seedlings at 4 inches, cut to 3

activities.name: Fall Nitrogen #1
activities.description: With or just after overseed germination, ~Sept 15 typical. Per soil test: 16-0-8 if P confirmed high (expected on Central Basin phosphatic limestone).

steps.name: Buy fall fertilizer per soil test result
steps.description: PGF Complete 16-0-8 if P is high; 16-4-8 only if the test says P is actually low

activities.name: Fall Nitrogen #2
activities.description: Grass still green but vertical growth stopped -- early to mid November, around/after first freeze (typically late Oct to early Nov here). The most important feeding of the year for root reserves.

activities.name: Winter Broadleaf Spray
activities.description: November pass on winter annuals while seedlings are small. Two gates: a day above 50F, and the new overseed must have been mowed 4x before any herbicide touches it.

steps.name: Buy selective broadleaf herbicide safe for fescue
steps.description: 2,4-D / dicamba / MCPP three-way mix; verify seedlings mowed 4x first

activities.name: Late-Winter Nitrogen
activities.description: Light nitrogen ~2 weeks before the green-up push. Late February in Murfreesboro.

activities.name: Late-Winter Broadleaf Spray
activities.description: Second pass on winter annuals (Feb/Mar) while they're still small. Needs a day above 50F.

activities.name: Spring Pre-Emergent App 1
activities.description: Soil averaging 55F at 2 inches several mornings running (daily-high proxy; forsythia bloom is the field cue). Typical window Feb 25 - Mar 15; down by ~Mar 10. Prodiamine at split rate -- app 2 follows 8-10 weeks later.

activities.name: Spring Pre-Emergent App 2
activities.description: Split second application 8-10 weeks after app 1 (mid-May typical). UT: lower rate twice extends residual control, which matters because Murfreesboro's crabgrass germination runs long into summer. Use dithiopyr instead of prodiamine if any crabgrass has already emerged.

steps.name: Check lawn for emerged crabgrass, buy dithiopyr if present

activities.name: Grub Preventer
activities.description: Chlorantraniliprole (GrubEx) ahead of June/July beetle egg-lay. Late April to May window. 2027 onward, annual.

activities.name: Todoist Sync Test
activities.description: Throwaway task validating the full pipeline early: trigger fire -> enqueue -> Todoist create -> completion poll-back. Complete this in Todoist when you see it; the system should mark it completed in the DB on the next morning run. Safe to ignore afterward.

steps.name: Confirm test tasks appeared, then complete both
